leads.jd:
Job Description: Manager-CEO's office 
 Role Overview: We are seeking a highly motivated and strategic thinker to join our team as a Strategy Associate/Manager. This role is pivotal in driving key initiatives and strategy projects that will shape the future of our organization. You will work closely with the CEO and leadership team to ensure rigor in problem-solving, strategic planning, and execution across various functions. This is meant to be a pre-MBA role, if you thrive in a fast-paced environment and are passionate about driving impactful change, this role is for you. Past Alumni have gotten admits at HBS, Wharton etc, Moved on to leadership roles at large MNCs.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Drive Strategic Projects: Lead critical strategy projects from 0->1 and 1->10, initiating and scaling new business initiatives across the organization.
 Org-level streamlining: Ensure timely interventions and rigorous problem-solving on key projects through close collaboration with leadership.
 Business Understanding & Metrics: Develop a deep understanding of the business and success metrics, tracking progress through detailed dashboards and analytics.
 Planning & Execution: Drive quarterly and annual planning cycles across the organization, and monitor execution through regular weekly reviews.
 Culture & Change Initiatives: Collaborate with functional and organizational leadership to drive initiatives that define and evolve the company culture.
 Qualification 
 Educational Background: Strong academic pedigree with an undergraduate degree from IITs/BITS 
 Experience: 
 2-4 years of experience in strategy consulting firms (MBB, ATK, Strategy&, Dalberg, Auctus), high-growth startups (Flipkart, Ola, Swiggy), or leading corporations (ITC, HUL, P&G).
 Demonstrable spike in academic or professional achievements.
 Skills & Attributes: 
 High degree of ownership and accountability.
 Strong aptitude and ability to quickly grasp new concepts and domains.
 Proven experience in structured problem-solving and stakeholder management.
 Ability to switch contexts and manage multiple priorities with passion, hunger, and perseverance.
 Desired Personal Traits: 
 Passionate about driving change and making an impact.
 Hunger for learning and growth, with the ability to persevere through challenges.
 Strong context-switching skills, comfortable navigating complex and dynamic environments.
 Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to manage and influence senior stakeholders.
 What We Offer: 
 Opportunity to work directly with senior leadership and have a meaningful impact on the organization’s strategic direction.
 A dynamic and entrepreneurial work environment where your ideas and contributions will be highly valued.
 Competitive compensation and benefits package.
 If you are a strategic thinker with a passion for solving complex problems and driving impactful change, we would love to hear from you!

 Millions of Indians talk to each other on FRND every day: one-on-one, in groups and in live rooms.  ⚡ You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking independent decisions and shipping before everything is perfect.
 💪 You have a strong bias for action and can manage multiple high-priority initiatives.
 🤖 You already use AI tools in your daily work and actively look for ways to improve workflows through automation.
 Note: The FRND team works 6 days a week, with 1st and 3rd Saturdays being working days.

 FRND is redefining the way people connect by building a social platform that’s not just engaging but also safe, inclusive, and fun . We’re a rapidly growing startup with a bold mission: to transform online interactions into meaningful relationships.

leads.title: Strategy and Operations Analyst
leads.jd:
Job Application for Strategy and Operations Analyst at Prodigal 
 Strategy and Operations Analyst
 Bengaluru
 Apply 
 About Prodigal 
 Prodigal is the connected AI platform leading financial institutions use to run their operations.
 We work with banks, lenders, credit unions, and other financial companies that lend money to people and manage those relationships over time.
 These institutions make millions of high-stakes decisions every day. Who should they reach? When should they reach them? What should they say or offer? When should a case move to a human? How should that change based on the borrower, the account, previous interactions, and the regulations involved?
 Getting those decisions right requires a deep understanding of the people, processes, rules, and edge cases behind them.
 Prodigal has spent the last eight years building that understanding. More than a billion interactions between financial institutions and their customers have shaped the intelligence, guardrails, and AI agents we now run in production across North America.
 Today, our AI agents analyze conversations, capture context, guide human agents, decide the next action, conduct customer conversations, orchestrate outreach, and help people complete payments and resolutions. They are connected, so what is learned in one interaction can inform what happens next.
 We are expanding this swarm of AI agents across more of the work financial institutions do: originations, document processing, back-office workflows, servicing, and other critical operations where money, identity, people, and regulation intersect.
 We are backed by Y Combinator, Accel, and Menlo Ventures, and work with 100+ financial institutions across North America. Listen directly from our CTO, Cofounder - Sangram Raje
 About The Team 
 You’ll join Prodigal’s Strategy & Operations team, the consulting arm of the company. We partner with creditors in consumer finance (Banks, NBFCs & BNPLs and debt collection agencies) to transform how they engage with consumers using data-driven insights and AI-powered workflows. The team sits at the intersection of product, data science, and client operations: designing strategy, building execution pipelines, and running experiments that deliver measurable lifts in recoveries and channel performance.
 Role Overview 
 As a Strategy & Operations Analyst, you will work with the team to execute and scale high-impact strategies and initiatives for clients. You’ll both build and scale: owning live AI based strategies, testing new ideas, identifying and solving client challenges, and driving strategic initiatives.
 This is beyond a traditional consulting role where impact ends at strategic recommendations. Here, you will own strategies end-to-end, from design to live execution. You’ll have visibility over their direct, measurable impact on real business outcomes. You’ll operate in a high-growth environment with accelerated learning, full ownership, and continuous exposure to CXOs. The role also offers periodic travel to the US for client meetings and industry conferences, giving you on-ground global exposure.
 This role is designed as a fast-growth pathway into a Strategy & Operations Lead position , based on performance, learning velocity, and leadership readiness.
 Mode of work - 5 days in office
 What makes you a good fit? 
 You enjoy solving real-world problems and taking full ownership of outcomes, not just analyses. You combine structured thinking with execution discipline and are comfortable working in fast-moving, client-facing environments. You’re motivated by measurable impact, continuous learning, and early responsibility. 
 Responsibilities 
 Strategy: 
 Act as a strategic advisor and industry expert to the CXOs of the customers you manage. They will rely on you for advice on what’s best for their business
 Own end-to-end engagement strategy, defining strategies to drive improvements in collections & recoveries, self-serve usage, and consumer experience
 Design structured experimentation frameworks by crafting hypotheses, choosing success metrics, and analyzing results to continuously refine strategy and inform scalable best practices
 Partner with data science teams to shape and operationalize models (e.g., channel affinity, right-time-to-contact, offer logic), ensuring strategies correctly leverage behavioral patterns
 Analytics and Operations: 
 Develop insightful, scalable reports and dashboards to track key performance metrics and proactively track deviations, trends, and anomalies
 Lead the execution and monitoring of A/B tests to measure product improvements and optimize service delivery
 Continuously improve underlying processes and systems by designing structured experiments, analyzing results, and translating learnings into scalable improvements
 Requirements 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Mathematics or a related field (Tier 1 college from 2025 batch preferred)
 Deep interest in consulting or product management
 Relevant data analytics experience
 Proficiency in Excel, Python, SQL, and Tableau/other BI tools is preferred
 Excellent communication skills (written and verbal), with the ability to clearly present findings to stakeholders and team members
 Evaluation Process : 
 Round 1 
 Intro and communication (15 minutes)
 Problem/puzzle solving (30 minutes)
 Case study (60 minutes)
 Round 2 
 Culture fit (20 minutes)
 Final Shortlist/Offer announcement
 Job Benefits: 
 World-class team - You'll get the chance to learn from (and teach) some of the brightest and most skilled people you'll ever meet. Our team members have been part of BCG, Deloitte, EY, Blackstone, Meta, Amazon and are IIT, IIM, BITS alumnus.
 Continuous education - As relentless seekers of knowledge, we sponsor and support any training materials, books, courses, and exam fees for upskilling yourself in areas related to your role - but that's not where it ends. If you make a good case for some extra learning, we're delighted to foot the tab.

 Senior Manager, CEO's Office
 Bangalore, Karnataka
 CEO Office – CEO Office /

 About the Role 
 Meesho's CEO's Office sits at the centre of how the company makes decisions. As Senior Manager, you'll work directly with the CEO and CXOs/GMs on company strategy, the operating rhythm, and the cross-functional bets that matter most.
 This is a leadership role, not a support role. You'll own outcomes, not just inputs. Scope will shift as company priorities shift, and you'll often work without formal authority. It suits someone who is part thinker, part builder, part operator.
 You'll get a front-row seat to building and scaling a public tech company, direct impact on the company's trajectory, and a launchpad for future leadership roles at Meesho.
 About the Team 
 The CEO's Office works as a force multiplier for the CEO. We run the company's operating system: the reviews, planning cycles and performance tracking that keep leaders aligned and accountable.
 We also pick up the problems that don't sit neatly inside one function. These cut across business, product, tech and operations, and we drive them to closure with the owners.
 It's a high-trust team. We see the company's most important decisions early, and we're expected to handle that with discretion and sound judgement.
 What you will do
 Partner with the CEO 
 Be a thought partner to the CEO: help pick, structure and drive the highest-impact priorities
 Speed up CEO decisions with sharp briefs, decision frameworks and analysis
 Represent the CEO in leadership forums when needed
 Run the company operating system 
 Design and evolve the operating cadence: reviews, planning cycles, performance tracking
 Improve clarity, alignment and accountability across leadership teams
 Make sure CEO and leadership decisions get followed through, with clear owners and dates
 Lead strategic, cross-functional projects 
 Lead high-impact projects across business, product, tech and operations
 Incubate and evaluate new business opportunities and adjacencies
 Take ambiguous problems, break them down, and turn them into plans that ship
 Work with CXOs and GMs to unblock and speed up key priorities
 Shape culture and leadership 
 Reinforce leadership principles and drive leadership communication
 Influence how decisions get made and how leaders work together
 Raise the bar on thinking quality and execution discipline
 What you will need
 Detail orientation. You think in specifics. You can walk through a P&L line by line, know the unit economics of the businesses you've worked on, and cite the numbers without being asked.
 Strong opinions. You take a clear position and defend it under pushback. You'll tell a senior leader what isn't working, including in your own team's work. You don't stop at "it depends".
 Curiosity. You ask the second and third question. You want to understand how the whole business works, not just your part of it, and you learn fast.
 Humility. Low ego, high accountability. You can name your own mistakes specifically, and you separate what you did from what your team did.
 Self-awareness. You know why you made each career move, what you're good at, and what you're not.
 Managerial style. You get results through others. You build systems rather than stepping in as the hero, and you've led across functions without formal authority.
 Must have 
 Strong structured problem solving and executive communication
 A record of solving complex, ambiguous business problems
 Proven cross-functional execution, with high ownership and bias to action
 Comfort working with senior leadership teams
 Strong advantage 
 Built or scaled tech products or businesses
 Startup or high-growth operating experience
 Founder's office, CEO office or strategy roles
 Close work with product and tech teams
 Marketplace, e-commerce or platform businesses

leads.title: APM - integrations
leads.jd:
WHO ARE WE?
Composio builds the AI-native automation layer for software teams: SDKs, runtimes, and platform tooling that let developers compose, evaluate, and operate agentic workflows and AI-powered products. Our systems must be reliable at scale - agents must act correctly, integrations must be robust, and integration needs to be an autonomous, observable function that accelerates engineering rather than slowing it. You'll join a small, high-leverage team building the delivery systems and metrics that give product and support teams visibility and predictable delivery.
This role is based in Bangalore (HSR).
WHO IS OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE?
A high-agency operator who is also AI-native, and who wants to grow into product. The role starts ops-heavy: you run the operations that get apps live on Composio, keep the toolkits healthy, and automate as much of that work as you can. Over 6-8 months, once those workflows and automations are running, the role shifts towards owning ambiguous product problems across the platform - triggers, tools, skills, auth, governance, and toolkit-level issues like rate limits and MCP hosting. This is not a traditional PM role with an engineering team to direct. It's closer to founder-mode ownership of a product line, where you solve problems using agents and a small ops team.
You've shipped things on your own - a side project, a tool, a micro-business, or a system you built that is still running - and you've run real operations with quality bars, not just executed inside someone else's process. You're at the edge of AI out of genuine curiosity: you use AI tools daily and can point to specific things you built or automated with them in the last month. You pick work by impact, not by how interesting it is, and you have no ego about manual work that isn't automated yet. You can hold a technical conversation with engineers without a translator, and you're comfortable owning problems that don't have a clear owner yet.
WHAT WILL THEY OWN?
 - The toolkit number: how many apps are live on Composio, and the health of the ones already live.
 - New apps, end to end: run the operations of getting them live - research, setup, QA, launch.
 - Existing toolkits: make them better with the product team, and clear the issues that stop them from working well.
 - QA and support for every toolkit you bring live. Once it's live, its quality is your problem.
 - The ops playbook: build it, run it, scale it. SOPs, small tools, AI agents before humans - you automate yourself first, and when scaling takes people, hiring them is part of the job.
 - The metrics for this function: define them, build them, watch them.
 - Product problems, as the ops layer starts running on its own: ambiguous, non-engineering problems across triggers, tools, auth, governance and toolkit-level issues - scoped, owned and shipped by you.
   
WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?
 - Experience: 2-4 years. We care more about how fast you've grown than how senior you are.
 - Technical floor: can explain what an API and an integration are, reads API docs cold, writes enough code to build small tools and automations. Not an engineer; infra-level work is not the job.
 - AI-native automation instinct: your default answer to repeated work is "how do I never do this manually again" - backed by recent, specific evidence of things you've built or automated with AI.
 - Dirty-work appetite: you happily run the manual version today while the automation is being built. This and the automation instinct are both required; we never average them.
 - Process maturity: you've designed or owned a pipeline with throughput, SLAs, or quality bars, and you left systems running behind you - not just stories.
 - Product instinct: you can take a vague problem, figure out what's actually broken, and decide what to build or fix - without waiting for a spec or a dedicated engineering team.
 - Organized ownership: routines, follow-ups, nothing dropped. You communicate clearly, in writing and in person.
 - High agency in uncertainty: given a goal with no playbook and no owner above you, you define the problem yourself and start before permission.
 - Operating maturity: this role carries a number from week one, so it needs someone who has owned outcomes before. It is not internship-shaped.
We'll pass at any stage on candidates who only want the cool parts of the job, choose work by interestingness over impact, can't explain what an API is, or do the same manual work in month three as month one.
NICE-TO-HAVE
 - Founder or early-stage experience: you've taken something from zero, or joined early and owned a function.
 - Experience with SaaS integrations, API products, or developer-facing products.
 - Built things with agents or LLM workflows beyond personal use - tools, experiment logs, side projects other people use.
 - An engineering-adjacent path: studied engineering and moved into non-technical work, or a non-CS background with things you built on the side.
 - High-throughput ops backgrounds (delivery, marketplace, physical ops) count only alongside the AI-native bar above - on their own they are not this job.
   
OUTCOMES WE EXPECT IN THE FIRST 90 DAYS
 - More toolkits live on Composio - you own the supply number, and it moved.
 - Existing toolkits repaired or unblocked without anything breaking technically.
 - A v1 ops playbook running: SOPs, automations, and AI agents handling the repeatable parts of onboarding and QA.
 - Metrics for the function defined and visible: supply, health of supply, pipeline status.
 - What this is not: usage. Usage is a product metric; this role is measured on supply and the health of supply.

leads.title: Product Manager - Chanakya
leads.jd:
About team: 

Chanakya is Sarvam AI's specialised, self-contained vertical for national security and institutions of national importance. It carries its own pricing, business, product, engineering, custom-model and vendor functions under one roof — a complete unit built to solve the most complex problems in the strategic sector: the three armed forces, intelligence agencies, financial regulators, and institutions of national importance such as central ministries and national policy bodies.

What we deploy here must be at strategic parity or higher — anything less is a national-security risk. That standard is the reason Chanakya is a small, exceptionally high-performing team inside Sarvam, and the reason we are deliberate about who joins it.

Why this is one of the most consequential seats in Indian AI

01 — NATIONAL IMPACT

You sit where it all gets decided.

These systems are deployed inside the institutions that safeguard the country. The potential for national impact is not abstract — it is at the core of how the strategic sector reasons, decides, and acts. Few roles anywhere in Indian technology carry this weight.

02 — UNPARALLELED LEARNING

Full-stack, end to end — nowhere else does this exist.

Every deployment runs the entire stack: understanding a customer's real requirement, architecting and customising the stack for it, and where needed building and fine-tuning models, shaping training data, and inventing data representations for extraordinarily complex data, workflows and applications. You touch nearly the whole arc of the work. This experience sets you apart — whether you go on to found a company, or become a business or technology leader in the years ahead, at Sarvam or beyond.

03 — A PATH TO LEADERSHIP

These are leadership seats in the making.

Chanakya's functions are being built out now. We are looking for people who will grow into the leaders of these emerging functions — every one of these roles is a route to leading a part of the vertical, not just filling it.

Where we are. This is not a leap into the unknown. Chanakya has already achieved product–market fit to a meaningful degree, has significant revenue booked, and has large strategic projects officially underway. Things are structured and going well.

The opportunity. This is a genuine zero-to-one journey — but one taken within the reach, talent and standing of a company like Sarvam. You get the ambition and ownership of building something new, backed by the full weight of Sarvam's capability and presence. leads.jd:
About:

The CEO's Office is a small, cross-functional team that incubates new products, drives the engagements that matter most to the company, and builds the systems that set and raise the bar for how teams across Sarvam work and collaborate. Problems arrive from research, product, and business, and they vary widely in shape and scope. As an Associate, you are a force multiplier for the CEO: you take an ambiguous problem, give it structure, and carry it to a result.

The work needs both breadth and depth. Breadth gives you context across the company and a clear sense of where the most important problems lie. Depth is how you deliver: you go deep on the ones that matter most and own their outcomes, working with the right people inside and outside Sarvam.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Drive 0-to-1 product and strategic bets from idea to a clear outcome, whether that ends in a working business line or a well-understood failure. The goal is to build an engine that comes up with ideas, researches and assesses them, builds and iterates on them, and takes the ones that work to steady state, often by handing them to a dedicated team.

 - Own key customer and partner engagements that are top of mind for the executive team.

 - Find new ways to use AI to set and raise the bar for how teams across Sarvam work and collaborate, and build the systems that make it happen.

 - Create the decks, memos, and prototypes that carry Sarvam's narrative to customers, partners, and government, and that represent the company.




WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - High agency: Ownership comes naturally to you. You drive work end to end, especially when the brief is ambiguous and the path is undefined.

 - Excessive curiosity: You are curious about AI and frontier technology well beyond what any job requires, and you follow new launches and research closely. You are eager to learn, and you are drawn to hard problems that new technology makes solvable.

 - Exceptional people skills: You write and speak clearly, collaborate well across teams, and build trust quickly, and you handle sensitive information with discretion. When a bet needs a team, you can lead it.

 - User obsession and agility: You start with the user’s pain points and reason from first principles about what would actually solve it. You use AI to build agents and products, and iterate quickly, and you keep going until you deliver real value and user delight.



What We’re Looking For

 - 2+ Years of work experience & a degree in engineering is preferred.

 - Excellent communicator: confident on demos, clear in writing, equally effective with a business stakeholder and an engineer.

 - Genuinely curious about AI: you want to understand how the models work, not just what they return, and you can characterise model errors with precision.

 - Organised and proactive: multiple threads in the air, nothing dropped, no prompting needed.

leads.title: Strategy & Operations Associate
leads.jd:
About Airbound
 Our mission is to make a world where everyone has access to delivery. Where goods move as freely as information moves today.
 This is possible. Today the cost of moving on a scooter is ₹2/km. That’s the cost of moving a 150kg mass from point A to B. We’re bringing that mass down to less than 5kgs, concurrently bringing the cost down to 10 paise/km. This is how we make deliveries a reality. This is how we create a world where we’re doing billions of deliveries per day.
The tech is not there. The current cost of drone delivery is ₹100/km. We need to completely redefine the way things are done here. We’re building the world’s most efficient aircraft from the ground-up, and scaling that up to beyond anything the aerospace sector has ever seen. This cannot be an iterative process. We have to tear down all conventions and build everything up from scratch.
To do this, we need nothing less than the best engineers. The ones who care about building something fundamentally different, who are deeply curious about understanding the fundamentals of everything they’re working on, who are dreamers that believe in the impossible.
 About Operations
 Operations run Airbound's fleet and makes sure every flight is safe, on time and cost-effective. At our stage it is a strategic pillar, not a support function: it drives growth and shapes what we build. The team owns launch-site selection and setup, flight planning, fleet utilisation and client onboarding. We monitor weather, collate flight data and mine historical patterns for predictive analytics, and we write the SOPs that keep the network safe. We also own the big-ticket problems, such as cost optimization and pricing strategy. Operations is the glue that holds Airbound together. We work with engineering to turn growth ambitions into a detailed operations roadmap that directly informs product design and engineering priorities. We decide with data, not instinct. We form hypotheses, then prove or disprove them with flight logs, delivery times and cost metrics. We are process-obsessed and biased toward fast execution, always asking how we can deliver better, faster and cheaper.
 About The Role
 The Strategy & Operations Associate works directly with the Chief of Staff and the Head of Operations on high-impact projects across the Ops team. A core part of the role is building operational and financial models that project costs under different scenarios and inform how we price our delivery services. The role is full-time and on-site (no remote work), with substantial room to grow within the company.
Key Responsibilities
 Financial modelling and pricing: Build and maintain Excel models that forecast operational costs (airframe, motor and servo life, maintenance, manpower) under different growth scenarios, and use them to guide pricing and resource allocation
 Operations roadmap: Work with R&D, Manufacturing and Software to turn growth plans into an operations roadmap, with clear problem statements, constraints and success metrics
 Data-driven improvement: Analyse delivery times and cost data to find bottlenecks, and propose fixes for routes, turnaround times and inventory
 Special projects: Lead or coordinate projects such as setting up new launch hubs, entering new regions or evaluating partnerships
 Leadership and investor reporting: Prepare concise presentations on operational plans, cost forecasts and performance metrics
 SOPs and compliance: Help review SOPs and safety protocols so processes stay scalable and compliant as we grow
 Ad-hoc support: Handle urgent analyses, competitive research, new business evaluations and the operations inputs to fundraising materials
 Qualifications
 Must-Have
 Bachelor's degree from a top-tier engineering school with a strong academic record. An MBA is not required
 1–2 years at a management consulting firm, an investment bank (front office, Industrials or M&A preferred), or in strategy/operations at a deep-tech startup. Quality of experience matters more than years
 Proven financial modelling and advanced Excel skills
 A structured problem-solver who is comfortable with ambiguity and turns complex problems into actionable plans
 Quick to learn new domains such as drone technology and aviation regulation
 Works well with engineers, pilots and business teams
 Clear written and verbal communicator, from technicians to the CEO to clients
 A self-starter with strong ownership and high attention to detail
 Genuine interest in UAVs, aviation, logistics and the future of delivery
 Good to Have
 Familiarity with SQL, Python or Tableau
 Experience coordinating cross-functional projects
 Work location: Hoskote, Bangalore (Headquarters)
 What We Offer
 Comprehensive health insurance to keep you and your loved ones covered
 Relocation assistance and a daily travel stipend to ease your commute
 Advanced salary credit to support you when you need it
 “A driven, passionate team where you’ll have room to grow and thrive - this is more than just a job, it’s a rare opportunity to build something meaningful from the ground up”
 Work Schedule
 In-office role, working alternate Saturdays.

What This Role Is
Every year, hundreds of thousands of students across India decide they want to study abroad. Some come through K12 school partnerships, some find their way in directly. When that journey works, a student ends up at a university that fits their budget, their course, and their ambitions, and the business realizes revenue at the moment they enroll. When it doesn't, applications stall, deadlines slip, and a student who could have enrolled goes quiet.
The problem is not that any single team is failing. It's that the highest-leverage work in a business like this doesn't live inside one function - it lives in the transformation and optimization projects that cut across Tech, Product, Marketing, and Operations, and someone needs to own them end to end. A funnel improvement that Marketing wants tested needs Product to build it and Tech to ship it. A new process that could remove a structural inefficiency needs someone to design it, prove it, and hand it off cleanly. Right now, that ownership happens informally, project by project, and the work that would compound doesn't get the sustained, disciplined execution it needs.
This is where this role sits. You will run multiple 'Strategize - Build - Operate - Transfer' projects a year - some of them genuinely 0-1 (new ideas that need user research, market research, and hypothesis testing before anyone knows if they work), some of them optimization projects on things that already exist but need better process design and a new benchmark for what good looks like. You will also be asked to take on whatever else is critical for the business to win, even when it doesn't have a job title yet.
You will own full-cycle delivery for these projects - from framing the problem with the right stakeholders, through build and testing, to launch, operating it long enough to prove it works, and transferring it cleanly to whoever owns it long-term. You are the person who makes sure a project doesn't just get discussed. It gets shipped, it gets proven, and it gets handed off in a state someone else can run with.

 Why this role matters
 For a salon owner, a booking is not a feature. It is their rent, their stylist's paycheck and their Saturday. When a booking goes wrong, a real person shows up to an empty chair or a client walks away frustrated. When a payment fails, a small business feels it the same day.

 Bookings

 Payments
 Online payments at the time of booking, including cards and digital wallets common in the US
 Checkout, tips, gift cards, packages and memberships

 Across both
 The roadmap, the metrics and the story of why we're building what we're building
 Making sure our AI and marketing products feed real bookings and real revenue, and that the data flows back to make them smarter

 Getting on calls with salon owners and front desk staff in the US to understand how they actually run their day
 Digging into booking funnels, failed payments and no show data to find where we're losing money for our customers

 Prioritising ruthlessly between new capability, reliability work and the bug that's annoying three of our biggest salons
 Listening to Customer Success and Sales, and turning what they hear into product decision

 We are looking for a highly driven, execution-oriented Founder's Office Associate to work closely with the founders across GTM, growth, hiring, marketing, and business operations. This is a high-ownership role for someone who enjoys moving between strategy and execution one day building an outbound pipeline, the next coordinating a hiring drive, refining a pitch deck, researching potential partners, or ensuring an important client deliverable gets shipped on time. You will operate as an extension of the founders and help turn priorities into measurable outcomes. The ideal candidate is resourceful, organized, commercially minded, a strong communicator, and comfortable working with ambiguity. You should be someone who doesn't wait for instructions for every task, can independently figure things out, and has a strong bias toward action.
 The candidate will have responsibilities across the following functions : 
 GTM and Growth: 
 Build and operate the growth engine for new products and offerings.
 Research markets, ICPs, competitors, customers, and relevant industry trends.
 Build and maintain weekly content calendars for LinkedIn and X.

 Manage the content workflow from idea drafting to review to publishing.
 Research high-quality accounts, founders, analysts, customers, and communities for thoughtful engagement.
 Maintain target-account and target-handle lists with relevant notes and follow-ups.
 Identify and research potential strategic partners, agencies, communities, technology platforms, and cloud marketplaces.
 Build and maintain partner pipelines and coordinate introductory conversations.
 Research prospective customers and decision-makers within defined ICPs.
 Create and execute structured email/LinkedIn outreach sequences.
 Track conversations, meetings, opportunities, and pipeline movement.
 Hiring and Talent Acquisition: 
 Help build a repeatable hiring engine for engineering and other priority roles.
 Campus Hiring:
 Identify colleges and institutions relevant to our talent requirements.
 Build relationships with placement teams, faculty, student communities, and technical clubs.
 Coordinate hackathons, guest sessions, projects, and other campus initiatives.
 Develop internship/fresher job descriptions and screening assignments.
 Maintain campus hiring calendars and applicant pipelines.
 Lateral Hiring:
 Research competitor and adjacent companies to identify relevant talent pools.
 Build targeted candidate lists for SDE1 SDE2 Senior SDE, and other priority roles.
 Develop personalised candidate outreach.
 Track response, screening, interview, and conversion metrics.
 First-Pass Screening:
 Conduct 20-30 minute candidate verification calls.
 Validate experience, technical exposure, communication, motivation, and CV accuracy.
 Maintain standardised screening notes and scorecards.
 Coordinate shortlisted candidates with the engineering team.
 Maintain a target turnaround time of 48 hours from recruiter handoff to recommendation.
 Marketing and Packaging: 
 Help convert company/product positioning into high-quality sales and marketing assets.
 Build and maintain the company's master pitch deck.
 Develop persona-specific versions for different customers and use cases.
 Coordinate with founders, engineering, research, and design teams to create compelling narratives.
 Maintain a library of product screenshots, diagrams, benchmarks, case studies, customer proof points, FAQs, and other assets.
 Coordinate with design partners to improve visual quality and consistency.
 Maintain brand and presentation standards.
 Coordinate website copy, page structure, assets, and landing-page launches.
 Work with design/development partners to ship new pages and offerings.
 Monitor basic website conversion metrics and coordinate CRO experiments.
 Founder's Office and Business Operations: 
 Support the founders in keeping high-priority initiatives moving.
 Track important company and client initiatives from start to finish.
 Coordinate meetings, follow-ups, documents, and action items.
 Maintain client trackers, milestones, owners, and deadlines.
 Ensure timely follow-up on internal and external commitments.
 Coordinate with engineering, product, recruiting, design, and external partners.
 Maintain meeting notes, decisions, documents, and operating repositories.
 Keep task boards and project trackers clean and up to date.
 Identify bottlenecks and escalate risks before they become problems.
 Help establish repeatable processes, templates, dashboards, and SOPs.
 What Success Looks Like: 
 Within the first 90 days, you should be able to:
 Establish a predictable content and GTM operating rhythm.
 Build initial partner and prospect pipelines.
 Run structured outbound campaigns and generate qualified conversations.
 Establish repeatable campus and lateral hiring pipelines.
 Conduct consistent first-pass candidate screening.
 Improve and maintain the company's pitch decks and marketing assets.
 Coordinate website and landing-page launches.
 Establish reliable tracking for key GTM, hiring, and operational metrics.
 Become a trusted execution partner to the founders.
 Key Metrics: 
 GTM and Growth

 Weekly pipeline and outreach reporting.

 Marketing assets delivered within agreed timelines.

 95% SLA adherence.

 Clear ownership and status visibility for priority initiatives.

 Technical Program Manager

 You will run the technical programs for a payment instrument: a set of partner capabilities, a mandate, or a merchant-facing area such as refunds, webhooks, or recurring payments. You make sure to work across engineering, banking alliances, segment PMs, and TAMs on time, on cost, and in a way merchants can actually use. You work every day with the EM(s) and staff engineers, who own the technical design and partner tech work.
 Responsibilities: 
 OKRs: Help set the payment instrument's program OKRs and own one or two key results for your area, for example, merchant integration time or a mandate deadline. Track them weekly and report progress.
 Requirements and plans: Turn asks from segment PMs, merchants, and compliance into clear requirements: use cases, merchant-facing behavior, edge cases, and acceptance criteria. Build the plan with the EM and keep it current.
 Partners and integrations: Work with banking alliances on which partner capabilities your area needs and what they cost. Make each integration succeed for merchants: the right pilot merchants, docs ready, TAM and sales briefed, and adoption tracked after go-live.
 APIs and SDKs: Know our merchant-facing APIs and SDKs well enough to answer most integration questions yourself. Review API specs for merchant integration experience. Own developer docs, integration guides, and merchant-facing error messages for your area.
 Mandates: Run the program for RBI, NPCI, and network circulars in your area; work out the impact with Compliance; hand clear requirements to the EM; and track it to the deadline.
 Cross-team work: Track dependencies on other teams, shared platform teams, risk and finance systems, and clear blockers early.
 Merchant and business sense: Understand the problem behind each request and the cost and merchant impact of each choice. Use data to show what matters most.
 What success looks like: 
 By 3 months: You know your team's flows and own the requirements, plans, and docs for your area.
 By 6 months: You have landed multiple initiatives on time, and merchants are adopting what shipped. Your key results are tracked weekly.
 By 12 months: Segment PMs, TAMs, and engineers come to you first for your area, and you have measurably improved merchant integration time or adoption.
 Requirements: 
 1-5 years in technical program management, solutions engineering, integration, or software engineering, ideally in payments or fintech.
 Comfortable reading API docs, making API calls (Postman or curl), reading JSON, and following a sequence diagram.
 Basic SQL to pull and analyze transaction and adoption data.
 Clear writing: requirements, plans, docs, and updates people can act on.
 Follow-through: you close loops across teams without reminders.
 Educational Qualifications: Graduation or post-graduation from a tier-1 engineering college.
 Nice to have: 
 Hands-on engineering experience, such as building a backend service or a merchant integration in the past.
 Familiarity with payment concepts: auth and capture, settlement, reconciliation, idempotency, webhooks, 3DS, tokenisation.
 Experience writing developer documentation.
 About Cashfree
 Cashfree Payments is a leader in payments in India. Founded in 2015 Cashfree Payments processes transactions worth $80B annually for more than 800,000 businesses. 
 Businesses use Cashfree Payments to collect payments from 100+ payment methods, make payouts, make cross-border payments, improve conversions with a one-click checkout, recover abandoned carts, and predict and reduce returns. With an easy onboarding and integration process, and compatibility with popular merchant platforms like Shopify, Wix, Wordpress, WooCommerce, WhatsApp, Cashfree Payments enables businesses to start transactions within a day. Cashfree Payments directly connects with all payment networks and owns its payment processing technology end-to-end, ensuring higher success rates and reliability. Built for scale, it enables businesses to process an industry-leading 12,000 transactions per second, handling peak demand effortlessly. 
 Alongside payments, Cashfree Payments offers SecureID, an identity verification stack with a comprehensive suite of APIs and KYC components. SecureID enables fintechs and startups to streamline compliant onboarding and KYC flows by minimising user inputs, thus reducing drop-offs, intelligently verifying identity documents, and detecting fraud and anomalies with high accuracy. 
 Cashfree Payments is authorised by the Reserve Bank of India to operate as a payment aggregator for both domestic and cross-border payments, and was one of the first entities to be authorised. It is also authorised to issue Prepaid Instruments. 
 Cashfree Payments is backed by Silicon Valley investor Y Combinator, Apis Partners, Krafton, State Bank of India (SBI), and was incubated by PayPal.

leads.company_note: YC Winter 2026 · team of 8 · AI video editor (raw footage into finished videos)
leads.title: Founder's Office (speculative note to founders)
leads.jd:
Cardboard (cardboard.ai) is an AI video editor that turns raw footage into finished videos, from social clips and highlight reels to product demos, launch videos and event recaps. Describe the video you want, and Cardboard turns your clips, photos, recordings or a link into an edit you can watch, change and export, in the browser, in the Mac app, or right inside ChatGPT and Claude. It pulls out the best moments, removes pauses and filler words, adds captions, titles, music and B-roll, and reframes for Reels, Shorts and TikTok. It’s built for marketing teams, founders and creators who need video every week without learning a timeline.

Say what you need, like “three 30-second ad variants” or “a customer testimonial from these interviews”, and Cardboard’s AI agent, Director, builds a first cut in minutes. You refine it by chatting or on a full timeline, with your team. Cardboard edits the footage you already have. Unlike AI video generators such as Runway or Sora, it doesn’t create new video from a text prompt.

- Recreate the style of a reference video with your own footage.
- Make motion graphics from a prompt, from animated titles to 3D scenes like a spinning product shot.
- Cut to the beat, with match cuts, transitions and effects synced to the music.
- 80+ ready-made recipes (templates) for videos like launch videos, product showcases, podcast clips, webinar highlights, and testimonials.
- Export the finished video, or hand the timeline off to Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.

Why now: AI models can finally understand video, and WebGPU makes a professional editor possible in a browser tab. Most AI video tools are either an old editor with AI bolted on, or an agent with no real editor behind it. Cardboard is built to be both.

Team: Saksham Aggarwal (CEO) and Ishan Sharma (CTO) have been friends for 15 years, since school. Saksham studied computer science at BITS Pilani, was co-founder and CTO of Iterate AI (backed by Entrepreneur First), and worked in growth at Sequoia-backed Flint. Ishan spent nearly five years building performance-critical browser apps at HackerRank (YC S11), and at 14 built Hotspoter, a Windows app with over 5 million downloads.

Together, they are unusually suited to build the editor core others avoid.

Video is becoming the default distribution channel, and the team that iterates fastest compounds attention. Cardboard becomes the default workspace for video production, the way Canva/Figma became the workspace for design - because it’s collaborative, fast, and does the tedious parts for you.

(formerly usecardboard.com or cardboard.sh)

SuperKalam: AI-Powered Super Mentor for Test Prep | Y Combinator 
 AI will eventually “be as good a tutor as any human ever could.” He cited, for example, the fact that most students can’t afford one-on-one private tutoring, leaving them without someone who can understand and adapt to their individual needs. Technology will ultimately fill that gap, AI-driven software will know your interests and your learning style so it can tailor content that will keep you engaged. It will measure your understanding. It will give immediate feedback, he said.

## **AI x Education = SuperKalam**

We have built SuperKalam by thinking how education & learning can be delivered in the AI-first world.

At SuperKalam, we harness AI to democratize education, making it affordable and tailored to each student's needs. As an AI-driven personal mentor, SuperKalam helps students excel in the highly competitive UPSC Civil Services Examination.

Guided by India’s top educators and the latest AI models, SuperKalam has already become the favorite personal mentor.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=81539&key=user_uploads/990441/393a67be-37ed-4037-815d-7e9eb074867a)

### [**Join Us for a LIVE Session with SuperKalam to Decode UPSC Prelims 2024**](https://superkalam.com/upsc-prelims-2024-answer-key)

The UPSC Prelims 2024 is scheduled for June 16th. As soon as the exam concludes at 4:30 PM, we will be hosting a LIVE session with SuperKalam AI and our expert team.

This session is designed to provide students with the Answer Key for UPSC Prelims 2024, detailed explanations, and real-time doubt resolution, apart from Standard Sources of the UPSC Prelims 2024 GS Questions.

Imagine getting instant feedback on the Prelims answers for UPSC 2024, understanding the nuances behind each question, and analyzing previous years' trends to better prepare for future attempts. This session is not just about getting answers; it's about learning and growing with each step.

> On June 16th at 5 PM, [**join here**](https://superkalam.com/upsc-prelims-2024-answer-key) for a one of a kind Free LIVE session where SuperKalam will solve the UPSC Prelims 2024 paper in real-time.

If you are UPSC 2024 or 2025/26 aspirant, [**click here**](https://superkalam.com/upsc-prelims-2024-answer-key) to:

* **Get the Answer Key for UPSC Prelims 2024**: Accurate and immediate.
* **Receive Detailed Explanations**: Understand the reasoning behind each answer.
* **Resolve Your Doubts in Real-Time**: Ask questions and get instant responses.
* **Analyze Trends**: Compare with previous years to spot patterns and prepare smarter.

> Whether you are looking for the GS Paper I Answers 2024 Prelims or want to solidify your preparation strategy for UPSC 2025-26, SuperKalam is here to guide you. Let's decode the UPSC Prelims 2024 together and set the stage for your success.

All the best.

Beyond classes, students participate in global coding competitions, hackathons like HPE CodeWars, and online coding camps, further nurturing their creativity, confidence, and innovative spirit. leads.company_note: YC Summer 2020 · team of 25 · Ecosystem Platform for Restaurants in India
leads.title: Data Analyst
leads.jd:
Explorex — The Memory Layer for Physical Commerce

~90% of Indian retail happens in person, yet offline venues have no memory of their customers. Restaurants run on disconnected tools, and every visit ends with zero data captured. Explorex fixes this by owning both sides of the dining transaction.

At the center is Elite, our consumer app that is redefining how people dine out. Diners see live table availability, browse dynamic menus, order, and self-checkout instantly — no waiting, no interruptions. Behind it sits our infrastructure stack: Bridge OS (the full-stack restaurant operating system), Clyro (WhatsApp-native CRM), and ReserveX — all feeding a single behavioral data layer.

That data layer is what makes Explorex fundamentally different. Delivery platforms only see orders. We capture real-world, in-venue behavior — what people order, how long they stay, how groups behave, how menus perform, how experiences shape spending. Because we operate the restaurant OS and the consumer touchpoint, this data is irreplicable.

We're now building Elara, an AI dining concierge that turns this data into real-time decision-making — factoring intent, context, availability, and historical behavior. This moves us beyond discovery into becoming the intelligence layer for offline commerce.

Today, Explorex powers 250+ partner restaurants and 3M+ diners across Bangalore and Hyderabad, processing 8M+ transactions annually (18M+ lifetime), and operates at breakeven.

Explorex is not a SaaS tool — it is the infrastructure layer for offline dining, with AI and consumer experience at its core. Think Shopify for restaurants, on its way to becoming the UPI of restaurant operations.
leads.exp_text: 3+ years experience

leads.jd:
👩‍💻 THE ROLE

We're looking for a sharp, hungry analyst to join the data team at Headout. This is a foundational role, you'll work closely with senior analysts and leadership to build the reports, dashboards, and automations that power decisions across the company.

Depending on where the need is greatest and where your strengths lie, you could find yourself working on growth and marketing analytics, product analytics, operations and supply-side problems, or a mix of all three. The common thread: you'll be embedded in the business, working on problems that matter.

This isn't about crunching numbers in a corner. You'll understand how our marketplace works, why metrics move, and what levers actually drive outcomes. You'll ship real work within your first week, and own meaningful workstreams within your first few months.

If you're someone who gets restless when you're not learning, who'd rather figure things out than wait for instructions, and who cares about craft, this is for you.


🤩 WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE SPECIAL?

 - Real problems, not busywork: Headout is a global marketplace operating across dozens of cities, thousands of experiences, multiple currencies, real-time inventory, and dynamic pricing. Whether you're analyzing conversion funnels, attribution models, supplier economics, or product experiments, the problems here are genuinely hard.

 - Breadth of exposure: You won't be siloed into one corner of the business. You'll see how growth, product, operations, and finance interconnect and build the analytical muscle to work across all of them.

 - Learn fast by doing: You'll pair with senior analysts on complex projects, get direct feedback from leadership, and see your work influence actual decisions. The feedback loops are tight, and the growth curve is steep.

 - A team that gives a damn: We care about speed and pragmatism over perfection, but we don't ship sloppy work. Feedback is direct and frequent. We document what we learn. We help each other get better.

 - A product you can care about: Headout helps people experience the best of every city they visit. There's something satisfying about working on a product where the output is someone having a great day somewhere new.


💝 WHAT SKILLS & EXPERIENCE DO YOU NEED?

 - 1 - 3 years in an analytics, BI, or data science role

 - Strong SQL skills, you can write complex joins, window functions, CTEs without hand-holding. You know how to debug a slow query.

 - Working knowledge of Python for data manipulation, automation, or simple analysis

 - Hands-on experience with at least one BI tool (Metabase, Looker, Tableau, Power BI)

 - Nice to have: exposure to dbt, Airflow, or similar; basic understanding of data warehousing concepts

 - Bonus: exposure to marketplace/e-commerce, consumer tech

 You will own the Ki score from India end to end. The KISS score gives lenders explainable credit decisions for people with little credit history, combining bureau, bank statement, GST, and alternate data with business rules to reach an approve or decline decision. You will decide where it goes next and how it is priced, as well as how it is built: the scoring API that lenders integrate with, the data and models behind it, and the new modules on top.
 The core responsibilities for the job include the following:
 Strategy, pricing, and prioritization: 
 Set the KPI score roadmap and decide what gets built first, weighing revenue, client commitments, and the effect on credit outcomes.
 Own pricing and costing for Ki Score and its modules, and build the commercial proposals that go to lenders with the sales team.
 Alternate data and research: 
 Go after data most lenders have never used, from satellite and geospatial signals to asset depreciation curves, farm-level data, and sources no one has tried yet. Find the ones that change who gets credit and on what terms.
 Lead the research: frame the hypothesis, test the lift with our data scientists, and put what works into production.
 Build out the alternate data lake that brings these sources together.
 Scoring platform and API: 
 Own the universal Ki score API and each lender's configuration of it, including the admin panel.
 Build self-serve tools, starting with a sandbox where lenders can test the KIS score on their own.
 Own the business rules engine (BRE) modules that sit on top of the models.
 Set up automated backtesting of models and policy rules.
 Lender deployments and models: 
 Own KI score deployments for our lending partners and for Kaleidofin's own NBFC, from data requirements through go-live and production monitoring.
 Work with the data science team on new model builds, including new asset classes, and decide what goes into production.
 Origination use cases: 
 Own income estimation and other origination use cases built on the KISS score.
 Own Account Aggregator data at origination, including the AA SDK.
 You will also define and track how the KISS score performs in production: approval rates at controlled risk, delinquency, turnaround time, and adoption.
 Requirements: 
 3 to 7 years of experience as a product manager on ML or data products, or as a data scientist. Data scientists looking to move into product management are welcome to apply.
 A working grasp of how credit or risk models are built, validated, and monitored in production.
 Commercial judgement: you can make the business case for what to build and help shape pricing.
 Comfortable with APIs and data: you can read an API spec, query data in SQL, and spot data quality problems.
 Able to turn an ambiguous problem into clear requirements that engineering and data science can build from.
 Clear communication with both technical and business audiences.
 Bonus (not mandatory): 
 Experience in credit underwriting, risk, or lending, ideally in India.
 Exposure to alternate data, account aggregator, or bureau data.
 About Kaleidofin
 Kaleidofin is a fintech focused on the goal to unlock access to tailored finance for women, agriculture and nano entrepreneurs. We provide the ki credit platform, combining credit health assessment (ki score), middleware rails and best-in-class risk management (ki view) to enable the financial ecosystem to better serve customers.  BharatNXT is a business payments platform on a mission to transform how Indian MSMEs manage their working capital. By enabling credit cards for business payments, we unlock liquidity and growth potential for entrepreneurs across the country.  Build partnerships - help find, evaluate and pitch new lending and payment partners. Once they're signed, keep integrations and timelines on track.

 Strengthen operations - build and fix the processes behind the company: vendor and partner agreements, renewals, finance and compliance follow-ups, and hiring support.

 What we're looking for 
 2 - 4 years at a startup, ideally working directly with founders and across several functions. 
 Structured thinking and clear writing - you can turn a messy problem into a plan, and a plan into a one-pager founders can decide on. 
 Comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities, and you follow through without being chased.

 Why take it

 If you want a 9-to-5 with a tightly defined scope, this isn't it. If you want a steep learning curve and problems that are yours to solve, it is.

Why this role exists 
The best product orgs don’t ship because of heroics – they ship because someone owns the machine that makes shipping happen. This role is that machine. You are the Head of Product’s leverage: you take the roadmap from intent to shipped, and make sure the most important product and tech bets land on time, at quality.
You are the right hand to the Head of Product – the person who turns product strategy into executed reality:
● What ships
● When it ships
● Whether it shipped well
 If your instinct is to build a tracker and stop there, this won’t work. If your instinct is to own the outcome until it’s done, read on. 
 What success looks like 
Not status updates. Not process for its own sake. Products ship – on time, at quality. The roadmap stays the roadmap. Product, Engineering, and Design move as one – on a rhythm, not on heroics.
 What will you own 
1. The Product Execution Engine: Own the rhythm that turns the roadmap into shipped product – sprint cadence, launch readiness, follow-through. Make sure decisions turn into action, and action turns into launches.
2. Roadmap & Program Management : Drive the most important product and tech initiatives end to end – across Product, Engineering, Design, GTM, and Category. Own the plan, the timeline, and the result.
3. Priority & Focus : Protect the roadmap from everything competing for the team’s attention. Make sure product energy goes to the bets that matter most – and stop the drift.
4. Unblocking : Find the bottleneck before it slips a launch. Align product and tech stakeholders, make the call or escalate it fast, and keep releases moving.
5. Truth & Tracking: Build honest visibility into milestones, tech sprints, and launches – dashboards and reviews that tell the truth, not a comfortable story. Surface slippage early, not late.
6. Product Leadership Rhythm: Run the product org’s rhythm of business – leadership reviews, sprint reviews, launch readiness. Turn every meeting into decisions and owned actions.
 Who you are 
● An operator who owns outcomes, not just plans
● AI-native in how you work – you use it to move faster and lighter
● Fluent with product and tech teams – you speak roadmap, sprint, and launch
● Organised without being bureaucratic
● High-agency – you drive without needing formal authority
● Direct and low-ego – you’ll say the hard thing and take the boring task
● 5–6 years in high-growth startups, tech/product companies, or consulting – with real exposure to
product/tech program management or cross-functional leadership
 What won’t work 
● Tracking work instead of owning it
● Process for the sake of process
● Hiding slippage until it’s too late
● Waiting for perfect clarity before you move

leads.location: Chennai or Bentonville or Arkansas or India or Singapore or Switzerland or United States
leads.jd:
Why this role exists
We're a founder-led company running two business lines across four countries. Things get committed to in meetings and Slack threads — and then don't close unless the CEO personally chases them. That's a cadence problem, not a talent problem, and it's the problem you're here to solve.
You will own the company's operating rhythm and drive decisions from made to done — across a senior leadership team you don't manage. When you're doing this well, follow-up becomes structural instead of the CEO's job. Fractional Chief of Staff 
 Company : Workday consulting + AI/SaaS products company (~40 people, US HQ)
 Location : Remote, US-anchored hours; team spans US, India, Singapore, and Switzerland
 Commitment : ~2–3 hours/day (fractional), monthly retainer
 Reports to : Founder & CEO Start: 60–90 day trial → ongoing
 What you'll own 
 Operating cadence. Design and run the weekly and monthly operating reviews: agenda, pre-reads, decisions logged, owners and dates assigned, progress tracked between meetings.
 Accountability tracking. Maintain a single source of truth for commitments across the leadership team. Know the status of every open loop and surface what's slipping before it's late.
 Follow-through, on the CEO's behalf. Chase progress with senior leaders — a revenue leader, a practice lead, a delivery lead, country heads — with the CEO's authority behind you, and without creating friction. Delivery is where commitments most often slip against client timelines, so keeping the delivery lead on track is a core part of the mandate.
 Meeting-to-action discipline. Turn leadership discussions into clear owners, deadlines, and next steps. Close the loop.
 CEO leverage. Prep the CEO for the week, flag what needs attention, and keep priorities visible so nothing important goes cold.
 Who you are 
 You've been a Chief of Staff, COO-lite, or head of operations at a 30–150 person company, ideally distributed / multi-timezone.
 You've held peers and senior leaders accountable — people who report to the CEO, not to you — and made it feel like help, not policing.
 You're systems-native: you think in cadences, trackers, decision logs, and owner/date discipline, not vision decks.
 You're comfortable with the ambiguity and pace of a founder-led company, and you close loops without being asked twice.
 You can operate across US and Asia-Pacific hours enough to keep a four-country team in sync.
 ​ 
 Nice to have 
 Exposure to professional services and/or B2B SaaS operating models.
 Experience standing up operating rhythm in a company that was scaling through your stage.

 AssistNow is a fast-growing digital transformation company specializing in:

Lenskart - Smart Generalist & EIR 
 Senior Manager - Business Strategy & Operations 
 About the Company 
 Lenskart is Asia's largest eyewear company, serving over 40 million people across 175+ cities in India, Singapore, Dubai, and beyond. What started as an online eyewear store in 2010 has grown into an omnichannel powerhouse with 3,000+ stores, the world's most automated eyewear manufacturing facility, and a mission to serve one billion eyes. \"Good is not good enough\" is something you'll hear often at Lenskart - we're constantly pushing ourselves to redefine how people see and experience the world.
 About the Role 
 This is an opportunity to solve some of the most important business problems at one of India's fastest-scaling consumer companies. As a Senior Manager – Business Strategy & Operations, you'll work directly on high-impact strategic initiatives that shape the future of Lenskart. You'll own critical workstreams, partner with senior leaders, and drive execution across multiple business functions. This role is designed for people who thrive in ambiguity, love solving complex problems, and want significantly more ownership than a traditional strategy role offers. Please note: After submitting your application, you will receive an AI assessment via email. Completing this assessment is mandatory for progressing to the next stage of the hiring process.
 Responsibilities 
 Own high-impact strategic initiatives from problem definition to execution, ensuring measurable business outcomes.
 Partner closely with business leaders to identify growth opportunities, solve operational challenges, and improve business performance.
 Drive cross-functional projects involving Sales, Retail, Supply Chain, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Customer Experience teams.
 Build business cases, perform deep analytical problem-solving, and convert insights into actionable recommendations.
 Leverage AI extensively for research, analysis, reporting, automation, and decision-making. Develop AI-powered workflows that improve productivity and eliminate manual processes wherever possible.
 Build dashboards, operating mechanisms, and review frameworks to track business performance and ensure execution excellence.
 Get hands-on with execution by working directly with business teams, stores, vendors, and stakeholders to understand problems firsthand and implement practical solutions.
 Present structured recommendations and updates to senior leadership through crisp communication and data-backed insights.
 Qualifications 
 Undergraduate degree from an IIT (or another top-tier engineering institute) and/or an MBA from an IIM or another leading global business school.
 2–5 years of experience in management consulting (McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Kearney, Strategy&, Oliver Wyman, etc.), investment banking, founder's office, CEO's office, business strategy, business operations, or high-growth startups.
 Strong analytical and structured problem-solving capabilities with experience handling complex, ambiguous business problems.
 Demonstrated ownership of high-impact projects with measurable business outcomes.
 Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority.
 Strong proficiency in Excel/Sheets, SQL (preferred), data analysis, and business storytelling.
 Daily user of AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Cursor, or similar) with the ability to build AI-assisted workflows, automations, or lightweight agents that improve business productivity.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to simplify complex ideas into clear recommendations.
 Founder, startup, or entrepreneurial experience will be considered a strong advantage.
 What You Can Expect 
 Ownership of business-critical initiatives with visible impact on the company's growth.
 Direct exposure to senior leadership and opportunities to influence key strategic decisions.
 A fast-paced, founder-led environment where exceptional performance is recognized with accelerated growth and responsibility.
 The opportunity to work across multiple business functions and gain a holistic understanding of scaling a global consumer brand.
 A culture that values first-principles thinking, speed, ownership, and continuous learning.
 The chance to build meaningful solutions using AI and modern technology while solving real business problems.
 A role that can become a defining milestone in your career—not because of the title, but because of the scale of problems you'll solve and the impact you'll create.
 Note: An AI assessment will be shared via email after application. Completing it is mandatory for progressing to the next stage.

Job Application for Founder’s Office: Revenue Operations & Systems (RevOps) at Enterpret 
 Back to jobs 
 Founder’s Office: Revenue Operations & Systems (RevOps)
 Bengaluru, Onsite
 Apply 
 About Enterpret
 As the world moves to AI native applications, one element matters more than anything: the data.
 At Enterpret, we are unlocking the most impactful dataset for businesses, customer feedback. We centralize feedback across every source, like Twitter, Salesforce, Zendesk, Slack, Intercom, community forums, surveys, and Gong calls, into a single knowledge graph. On top of it we build an adaptive taxonomy for each customer and an agent platform that lets teams query, monitor, and act on customer intelligence wherever they work, whether that's inside Enterpret, in Slack, or in their own AI tools through our MCP server.
 Our customers include companies like Canva, Harvey, Zapier, WisprFlow, ElevenLabs, OpenRouter, Western Union, and several other Product Led Growth decacorns and F500 companies.
 About the role
 Enterpret is looking for a sharp, data-driven operator to drive high-impact strategic and operational initiatives across the company, with a primary focus on revenue operations and business systems.
 As a member of our BizOps team reporting to the Chief of Staff to the Co-Founder, whose portfolio spans Business Operations and Product Operations, you will operate at the intersection of operations, finance, and GTM as a trusted problem solver and thought partner to teams across the business.
 This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role for an experienced individual contributor who enjoys solving hard problems and building systems that work. You will understand priorities, recommend solutions and take work from an unclear starting point to a working result.
 You will own and improve the workflows that connect our Sales, Marketing and Customer Success teams. This includes how leads reach the right person, how opportunities move through the pipeline, how teams use reliable data and how approved commercial terms flow into operational systems.
 We use AI as part of how we work. We want someone who can use it to learn, analyse, build and automate, while staying accountable for accuracy and quality.
 Why this role
 You will have real ownership of revenue workflows and the autonomy to improve how they work. Working directly with the Chief of Staff and closely partnering with the Head of Revenue and CEO, you will shape the systems behind our revenue operations and see the impact of your work.
 What you will do
 Proactively identify problems in our revenue workflows, recommend what matters most and own improvements through to measurable results.
 Own and improve core revenue workflows, including lead routing, opportunity management, renewals and the handoffs between teams.
 Understand our CRM and connected systems well enough to find the cause of issues, fix them safely and prevent them from recurring.
 Keep revenue data reliable. Define metrics clearly, reconcile conflicting records and build reporting people can use to make decisions.
 Support pipeline reviews, forecasting and quarterly planning with accurate inputs, clear risks and useful recommendations.
 Work with Finance and commercial teams to keep approved deal terms, subscription records and billing handoffs aligned. Help resolve exceptions without making policy or financial commitments on your own.
 Build useful automations and AI-assisted workflows. Test them with real users, monitor their results and improve them after launch.
 Drive cross-functional work forward. Agree on owners and dates, raise blockers early and bring the right people together when a decision is needed.
 Leave behind clear documentation and maintainable systems, not solutions that depend on one person remembering how they work.
 What we are looking for
 Experience owning revenue operations, business systems or closely related operational work. You can show work you personally took from problem to result.
 Hands-on experience with a CRM such as Salesforce or HubSpot and the workflows around it. You can explain more than the dashboard layer.
 Strong analytical skills. You are comfortable working with spreadsheets and SQL, checking data quality and explaining what the numbers mean.
 The ability to build and troubleshoot integrations or automations using APIs, tools such as n8n or Zapier, or lightweight code.
 Practical use of AI tools and agents, with a clear method for checking their output and measuring whether they help.
 Curiosity, sound judgment and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems quickly.
 Clear, concise communication and the confidence to work directly with people across teams and levels.
 A habit of following through. You keep people informed and verify that a change actually worked.
 We welcome relevant experience from different backgrounds. The strongest evidence is the work you have owned and the judgment you brought to it.
 Why Enterpret
 High Impact: Own the heaviest data systems in the company — the databases, models, and pipelines behind the product — at the moment the scale story gets much more interesting: larger enterprise customers and large-scale PLG volume.
 Ownership: End-to-end responsibility for features and systems.
 Complex Challenges: Make hard-to-reverse, 1–2 year architecture decisions across distributed databases, model hosting, and high-throughput pipelines, where a single change touches storage, query paths, reliability, and cost.
 Growth: Lead future programs such as self-hosting and regional expansion to Europe and India, with an open L6 IC path for someone who can own long-term platform strategy and raise the bar across the team.
 Culture: Open, collaborative, and values-driven environment with autonomy.
 Benefits: Competitive salary, equity, hybrid work setup, premium healthcare, and more.
 What We Value
 At Enterpret, we operate with a deep sense of ownership — we play for the team and do what it takes to win together. We care personally for our teammates while pushing each other with honest, actionable feedback. Above all, we approach everything with humility and a drive to keep learning and getting better.
 Equal Opportunities
 We are an equal opportunity employer. We ensure that none of our employees or prospective employees receives less favourable treatment as a result of age, sex, disability, marital status, colour, race, religion or ethnic origin. Equally we aim to ensure that no such employee is disadvantaged by terms and conditions of employment which cannot be justified.

Senior Associate / Assistant Manager, Strategic Initiatives (Founder's Office) 
 The Short version 
 Who we're looking for: A sharp, high-intensity problem solver with 3 to 6 years of experience, who cares deeply about education and is happiest when handed a messy problem with no playbook.
 What the role is about: You'll work directly with our CEO on the strategic priorities that will shape Kraftshala's next phase of growth, across admissions, training, placements, tech, partnerships, and scale, and you'll own each one from start to finish.
 Why you should apply: You'll work on some of the hardest and most critical problems in the company, alongside people with extraordinary expertise in skilling and training. There's a lot to learn here, and plenty of room to grow.
 About Us: Kraftshala is India’s largest skilling institution in terms of marketing placements, with a 94% placement rate, and we are gunning to become the world’s largest career launchpad, across domains.
 We’re backed by a number of eminent investors including ex-unicorn startup founders and CXOs of global giants like RedBus, NoBroker, Nestlé, and Performics.
 The Detailed Version 
 Our goal is simple: drive placements. That takes stellar admissions, training and placement processes, strong technology and deep partnerships across the ecosystem, and keeping all of it stellar as our programs grow. This role exists to solve the cross-functional problems that get in the way of that, working alongside the founder as priorities shift.
 Responsibilities & Metrics to Measure: 
 Take ambiguous, high-priority problems from the founder, break them down, find root causes using data, and turn them into a clear plan with owners and timelines.
 Spot where our programs risk slipping into mediocrity as they scale, across learner outcomes, placement quality and delivery standards, and fix the gaps at a system level.
 Run small, quick experiments on problem areas as they come up, share what worked and what didn't, and change course when the data or priorities shift.
 Act as the founder's thinking partner through sharp analyses, decision memos and reviews, and turn solved problems into repeatable processes that teams can run on their own.
 Top Grading
 Proactiveness: An A-Player spots the next problem before being told and moves on it, whereas a B-Player waits for direction and does well only once the task is clearly defined.
 Intensity & Focus: An A-Player attacks the most important problem with urgency until it's solved, whereas a B-Player spreads effort thin and lets momentum fade after the first push.
 Structuring Ambiguity: An A-Player turns a vague, messy problem into a clear problem statement, hypothesis and plan, whereas a B-Player either waits for clarity or jumps into action without a frame.
 Iterative Learning: An A-Player tests fast, learns from what didn't work and changes course without ego, whereas a B-Player sticks to the original plan even when the data says otherwise.
